summary: Honoré-Joseph Chavée was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven under Félix Nève and also under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the Royal Military Academy, Collège Stanislas de Paris, and Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa.

Honsho Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Minobusan Junior College as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992), Minobusan University (attested 1996), and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia as director (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University by 2004, having studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Arthur Rose was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at St Paul's School and Emmanuel College (~1886–1888), and later served in the Indian Civil Service from 1888 to 1917.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He studied at Queens' College and SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden. He served as Field Director for the Greater India Society and Vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied under Henry Thomas Colebrooke. He served as Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint, Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860), and Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (1837–1860).

Horace Irvin Poleman worked in Indology, studying at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, the US Embassy in New Delhi, and the Library of Congress, heading its Oriental Division (1955–1965).

Horace L. Friess was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University and Heidelberg University, and spent much of his career at Columbia University, where he became Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor of Human Relations (1962–1966).
Horkhang Sonam Palbar was a scholar in Tibetology. He studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang and Gendun Chophel (~1946–1951).
Horst Brinkhaus is an Indology scholar. He held an academic post at the University of Münster (~1978–1988) and later served at Kiel University (~1988–2011).

Horst Fichtner was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a Dr. med. from the University of Leipzig (~1920–1924) and taught social ethics at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1945.

Horst Lasic is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999, where he became a lecturer in 1999, and also worked as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India as Assistant Superintendent for Epigraphy (~1904–1920) and later as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).

Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Leigh studied under Ha-u Kim and the traditional teacher Cheonghwa, and earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoseong Kim is a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Kim founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo and has served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who spent his academic career at Koyasan University, where he served as a professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004).

Hotetsu Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held an affiliation at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and a professorship and directorship at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Hoyo Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961). He spent his career at Rissho University as a professor (~1975–2004), dean of Buddhist studies (attested 1984–1985), and special honorary professor (~2004–2021).
Hozen Seki was a scholar of Buddhist studies who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied in Paris and Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet, later holding positions at the Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University.
